10	
11	1. **1.8–7.0 s:** The two cards are identical empty boxes. Nothing shows "lower payment kept for a bad month." Fix: hang a smaller bill stack under the 30-year card and a taller one under the 15-year card. On "bad month" (6.8 s), add a storm cloud or darkened window, and have the 30-year stack drop down to its lower minimum.
12	2. **9.1 s:** The cards are gone and the tiles haven't arrived, which leaves dead time. The scene is a tiny figure in a black void, and the "Tessa" label is bigger than she is. Fix: start the pull-back and tile strip on "replayed" (9.4 s), and keep the cards visible until then.

14	4. **16.4 s:** "each extra dollar of principal earns" is carried by a dollar the size of a thumbnail. The caption fades to unreadable while it's still visible. Fix: push in on Tessa as she drops a bill onto the 30-year stack and the stack visibly shrinks. Fully clear the faded caption.

19	Emotion 2 · Sound-off 3 · Pacing 2 · Composition 3

Keep the cards up through 20.2 s, then start pushing the camera toward the house or begin bringing in the S04 bars.
24	4. **Throughout:** "ILLUSTRATIVE" appears twice, once in the corner and again in Tessa's name tag. Tessa is also tiny and turned away, so the scene has no emotional hook. Change her tag to just "Tessa", and turn her toward the cards so she seems to be looking at the rates.

29	1. **1.8 s:** A blank bar with no label sits alone on the right while Tessa and the house drift to the far left edge. The brief asks for bars over Tessa, not away from her. Keep her centered and grow the bars up behind or above her.

37	Scores: emotion/story 2, sound-off clarity 2, pacing 1, composition 2
38	
39	- **2.65 s:** The bars have no labels, so with the sound off nobody can tell which bar is the 15-year and which is the 30-year. The caption "$613 a month lower" also doesn't say lower than what. Fix: add the "15-year" / "30-year" base tags here, as S06 already has them.
40	- **8.1–26.5 s:** The camera swings to an oblique wide shot, and then nothing changes for about 18 s. The bars shrink to a corner and "fallback" becomes small. "Tight month," "job change," "big repair" and "squeeze" get no picture at all. Fix: show the pressure. A wrench or repair icon and a briefcase drop onto Tessa's budget, push the taller payment bar's top down against a ceiling line, and the green fallback block visibly absorbs it.
41	- **17.6–25.0 s:** "Wants the house paid off in 15 years" has no image. Tessa's only action is a small gesture at the house. Fix: put a 15-year finish line or calendar marker beside the bars, and have Tessa walk toward it. That sets up S06's raise.
42	- **8–26 s:** The oblique angle tucks the green block behind the left bar, so the gap is hard to read. Fix: keep the front-on framing, or push in on the bars instead of pulling wide.

45	Scores: emotion/story 3, sound-off clarity 4, pacing 3, composition 3
46	
47	- **2.7 s:** The bar is already raised and "$2,948" is already on screen, about 3 s before the narrator says the number (5.4–8.0 s). Fix: animate the 30-year bar rising from its old height during 2.4–5.4 s ("finishing that loan in 15 years") and land it on "$2,948."
48	- **8–13 s:** The $120 sliver is only a few pixels tall, so the payoff of the scene is hard to see. Fix: push the camera in on the bar tops while "$120 more" is spoken (10.3–12.2 s), then pull back.
49	- **18.88 s:** One bill floats with no stack and no destination in view, so "month after month" doesn't read. Fix: put the stack base in frame from 18 s on, place it next to the bars, and show a steady stream of bills (with a month counter on the stack) falling from the sliver.
50	- **24.27 s:** The stack is jammed against the house sign. Its two-line label takes the spot the "$2,828" tag used to hold, and that tag is now gone. Fix: move the stack between the house and the bars with clear space around it, and keep the $2,828 tag.

52	**S07 (17.7 s)**
53	Scores: Emotion 2 · Sound-off 2 · Pacing 2 · Composition 2

55	1. **1.8 s:** The stack is already standing when "stack of bills" is spoken at 2.1 s, so the reveal is lost. The two white pillars on the right are unexplained, and the ILLUSTRATIVE badge clips them. Fix: start with only the house and Tessa, grow the stack on "stack" at 2.1 s, and cut or explain the pillars.
56	2. **8.9 s:** The frame is empty black during "because the thirty-year carries…". It's dead time on the causal line of the scene. Fix: have the stack slide or morph into the space between the two rate lines, so the object becomes the gap with no cut.
57	3. **12.4 s:** The rate lines are drawing on unlabeled and fill only the left 45% of the frame. They also run off the left edge, and the right half is empty. Fix: center the chart, bring it in from the frame margin, and show the two lines in different accent colors from their first frame.
58	4. **16.0 s:** The gap bracket is tiny compared with the chart. The stack is gold here, but S08 uses green bills, which breaks continuity. Fix: put a small gold stack inside the bracket so "0.67 point" reads as the same object, and use one bill color across both scenes.

61	Scores: Emotion 2 · Sound-off 3 · Pacing 3 · Composition 3
62	
63	1. **1.7 s:** A short green stack and the cropped white pillars appear with no context, and Tessa and her house are gone. Fix: keep Tessa's house in frame so the money belongs to her. Cut the pillars or reuse them as the two loan terms.
64	2. **5.1–8.5 s:** The tall stack stays frozen for 3.4 s after it reaches full height. Fix: keep it rising slowly until "interest" at 8.5 s, or slow-push the camera up to its top.

But the 15-year is the short stack on the right, so the two closest labels read as one muddle. Fix: put each label straight above its own stack, at the same height and colour, with the leader lines going down.

76	4. **25.5 s:** At "October eighth unusual?", unlabelled grey slabs fade in (S10 pre-roll) and look like clutter. The two white pillars on the right are also never explained. Fix: show a single calendar-week tile under the house at 24.8 s, and remove or label the pillars.

Also, "how it was built is on screen" (29.7 s) has no method shown at all; add a one-line formula card there.

88	1. **1.44 s:** A grey grid of tiles from the last scene sits over the two rate lines, and the "Tessa's week = the last" pointer is still there. The opening frame is cluttered and confusing. Fix: clear the grid and the pointer before 0.5 s so the two lines start on a clean field.

103	1. **4.58 s:** The bars are drawn, but nothing ties them to "the gap", and no ribbon runs along their tops. The blue-to-gold colour change at 2.75 s happens on "stacks" and doesn't explain anything. **Fix:** grow the stacks left to right in time with "every week". Then run a bright ribbon along the tops on "rise and fall" (3.0–4.2 s) so the line moves with the words.

105	3. **6.42–9.2 s:** Frames 4 and 5 are identical, so about 2.8 s is a frozen shot. **Fix:** on "smallest" (5.4 s), push the camera in or dim every other stack, and let the marked stack pulse on "six thousand".

111	1. **0.5 s:** The "tallest" label is already fully on screen before "twenty-nine" (0.9 s), so it gives away the number. **Fix:** bring the marker in on "tallest" (0.2 s) and count the number up through "two dollars" (3.0–3.3 s).
112	2. **0.5–5.0 s:** All five frames are the same, which makes this a static 5-second shot. **Fix:** move the camera from the smallest stack to the tallest one so the viewer sees the spread between them.

114	4. **1.5 s:** The two labels are stacked close together and the "smallest" label sits far from its bar. This makes the top-right busy and pulls the eye away from the bars. **Fix:** fade the "smallest" label to a small tag on its bar when "tallest" comes in, so only the tallest label is large.

119	1. **2.07 s:** The median is spoken at 1.1 s, but its label doesn't appear until about 6 s. Meanwhile the leftover "tallest: $29,502 · Jan 2023" callout from the last scene pulls the eye to the wrong bar. Fix: remove the tallest callout at the cut, and brighten or pulse the median line itself at 1.1 s. That brightened line can carry the $16,631.

But Tessa's stack is at the left end, not the right end as intended, so the comparison runs against the reading direction. Fix: put her stack after 2023 at the right end, so the dashed line runs back across history to it.

Show the value only on her stack, not in the top block, and run the median line to the end of the row.
122	4. **18.6 s:** The brief says "Hold," but the camera pushes into a low angle and the median line, dashed line and lit/unlit contrast all disappear. Fix: keep the hold. For "can't measure," fade only the history row to grey and leave Tessa and her stack lit.

127	1. **1.11 s:** The camera pullback leaves the top half of the frame empty and the row small. Fix: frame tighter on the row so the four gaps open large in the centre.
128	2. **5.53 s:** A blue line appears with no key, and nothing on screen shows the pattern the narration says is unexpected. Fix: either cut the line or make it the payoff: draw it at "pattern" (2.1 s) and add a short key on the line.

The rest (7.75–9.96 s) is a dead hold, so begin the drop at "typical" (6.1 s).

135	1. 2.5–5.9 s: The 2000s stack reaches full height by 2.5 s, but its label only shows up somewhere between 4.2 and 5.9 s. "Fourteen thousand" is spoken at 4.3 s. That leaves about 3 s where nothing changes. Fix: make the stack grow more slowly so it finishes on "same" at 3.3 s. Pop the label at 4.3 s.
136	2. 2.5–7.5 s: Nothing in the picture says the two stacks are "about the same," and the frames look nearly identical. Fix: draw the dashed level line from the top of the 1990s stack over to the 2000s stack here, at about 3.3 s, instead of waiting until S18. Then S18 can reuse it.

144	2. 2.8–4.4 s: The dashed comparison line shows up at about 4.4 s, after "yet…cost more" (2.8–4.0 s). The surprise beat lands late. Fix: snap the dashed line on at 3.0 s and have the stack visibly grow up past it.
145	3. 4.8–6.1 s: The large header and the stack label both show $20,374, and both appear somewhere between 4.4 and 6.1 s. The number is shown twice. Fix: use a single label, timed to "twenty" at 4.8 s, and move the rate figure (4.03%) next to the line.

No gap brackets appear until about 9.9 s, so the picture is static through "gap" (0.8 s), "2010s and 2020s" (2.1–3.0 s) and "0.7 point" (5.3–6.4 s). **Fix:** On "gap" (0.8 s), grow the 2010s and 2020s brackets first and make them visibly wider. 161	1. **1.6 s:** The headline "2020s: typical stack $21,345" repeats the stack label right below it, so the same number appears twice. **Fix:** Drop the headline and push the camera in on the 2020s stack instead.

165	===== S21+S22 0.17559629999999998
166	I opened all 10 frames. Overall: S21 lands its main beat, but S22 never shows the picture it promises.
167	
168	**S21: emotion 3, sound-off 3, pacing 2, composition 3**
169	
170	1. **2.52 s:** The frame is empty. There's only the house, Tessa and a lot of black, while the narration has already started on the "shortcut." Fix: have the 180-tile track already laid out at 0 s, or have it grow out of the door by about 1.5 s.
171	2. **7.57 → 12.62 s:** The track sits at an oblique angle, then cuts to a straight-on view with an end wall. The jump in angle resets the viewer's sense of space, and the 180-month wall only appears at 12.6 s. Fix: open on the straight-on angle and keep it, with the wall visible from "fifteen-year" (6.9 s).
172	3. **17.66 s:** The 15 amber overrun tiles work well. But the dollar chips piling up at the left edge and on the house look like clutter. The "about 15 months late" label is dim amber on black. Fix: lose the chips here, raise the amber tiles slightly so they cast shadows, and brighten the label.
173	4. **22.71 s:** The "thin extra slab" is just a tiny green dot on each tile, so you can't see the extra payment as a layer. The amber tiles simply vanish, and a two-line caption carries the point. Fix: stack a visibly thicker contrasting slab on each tile, then animate the track pulling back to the wall as the amber tiles retract. Also, "history, not a forecast" in the footer reads oddly over loan math that looks forward.
174	
175	**S22: emotion 2, sound-off 2, pacing 2, composition 2**
176	
177	1. **2.0–18 s:** The intended chart isn't there. There's no flat payment line running over years and no balance shrinking under it. The thin bar under the grid doesn't read as a payment level. Fix: draw a horizontal ink-muted line above a balance bar or terrain that visibly steps down, month after month, while the line stays flat.
